Op.description: One change to the window's tree, as a tuple with its name first.

oneOf.description: `["createElement", id, type]`: a new element, not yet in the tree.
`["destroyElement", id]`: removes the element and everything under it.
`["appendChild", parentId, childId]`: moves the child to be the parent's last.
`["insertBefore", parentId, childId, beforeId]`: moves the child to be just before `beforeId`.
`["setStyle", id, style]`: the element's whole style.
`["setText", id, content]`: a text element's text.
`["setEventListener", id, eventType, hasHandler]`: whether the UI listens for an event on the element.
`["setRoot", id]`: the element the window draws.
`["setKeyboardFocusDim", enabled]`: whether controls dim while another has keyboard focus.
`["setCustomProp", id, key, value]`: any other prop, as JSON; `null` unsets it.

ElementId.description: An element's id: unique within its window, picked by the UI. 0 is the window.

zIndex.description: Paint order among siblings: higher paints (and hit-tests) later. Ties keep tree order.

imageRendering.description: `"pixelated"` samples this element's images (background, frame, ``) by nearest neighbour, for pixel art. `"auto"` smooths them.

rotate.description:
An `<svg>`'s turn about its centre, in degrees, clockwise: it moves neither its layout nor
where it is hit.

borderTopColor.description: One side's colour, over `borderColor`: bevels, inset and outset frames.

aspectRatio.description: Width divided by height, applied to whichever axis is not definite.

outlineWidth.description:
CSS `outline`: a line outside the border box that takes no layout
space, so it can appear on focus without moving anything.

scrollbarColor.description:
Thumb colour for a container that scrolls (`overflow: "scroll"`). Setting
it is what turns the native scrollbar on.

scrollbarWidth.description: Thickness of that thumb in px. Defaults to 6.

appRegion.description:
`"drag"`: the window moves by this element (a title bar of the app's own); `"no-drag"`:
not by this part of one.

pointerEvents.description:
`"auto"` blocks mouse hits behind this element. `"none"` never does.
Unset: block when this element paints a fill or is absolutely positioned.

selectionColor.description:
Selection wash colour for this subtree. Defaults to the theme accent at
35% opacity, the same tone Comet uses.

focusVisible.description: While focused after keyboard input, like CSS `:focus-visible`.

keyboardFocusDim.description:
`false` keeps this element at full opacity while another control has
keyboard focus. Not inherited.

StyleDesc.description: An element's style: what `setStyle` sets. Every field is optional; one left out is unset.

DimensionValue.description: Pixels as a number, or a string: `"auto"`, a percentage (`"50%"`) or pixels (`"12px"`, `"12"`).

anyOf.description: Painted like CSS: the first layer on top.

oneOf.description: Two stops paint natively; more are rasterised.
`center` is a fraction of the box (`[0.5, 0.5]` by default).
`angle` is where the sweep starts, in degrees clockwise from the top.

LinearGradientStopValue.description: One colour stop. A stop without a position sits evenly between its neighbours, like CSS.

RadiusValue.description:
A radial gradient's size: one radius (a circle), `[x, y]` radii, or omitted for the
farthest corner.

BackgroundLayerValue.description: One layer of a layered `background`: a colour or a gradient.

BackgroundImageValue.description: `backgroundImage`: a src, a layer, or layers (the first on top).

BackgroundImageLayer.description:
One image layer of `backgroundImage`. What a layer leaves out comes from the element's
`backgroundSize`, `backgroundRepeat` and `backgroundPosition`.

LengthValue.description: A length that is pixels (a number), a percentage (`"50%"`) or a keyword.

repeat.description: `"stretch"` (default), `"repeat"` or `"round"`, for the edges and the middle.

outset.description: Draws the frame this far outside the border box.

BorderImageValue.description:
A nine-slice image drawn as the element's frame (CSS `border-image`). `slice` is in the
image's pixels, `width` in the window's (the slice by default). The middle is drawn too
unless `fill` is false.

SidesValue.description: Four sides in CSS order: one value, `[vertical, horizontal]`, or `[top, right, bottom, left]`.

BoxShadowValues.description: `boxShadow` is one shadow or a list of them, painted in the order given.

inset.description: Draws inside the border box instead of around it, like CSS `inset`.

FontWeightValue.description: Font weight value: a CSS keyword or numeric string (`"bold"`, `"700"`) or a number (`700`).

oneOf.description: A primary-button click, or an assistive technology's press (with no position).
A click of another button.

pressedButton.description: The button held down, if one is: 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right, 3 back/forward.

oneOf.description: A press anywhere but on the element: what closes a menu.

precise.description: Pixel-precise (a trackpad), or by lines (a mouse wheel).

oneOf.description: The wheel or a trackpad. `delta` is in pixels (a line is 20).
Files dropped from the OS on the element: absolute paths.
The field's value changed (typing, a paste, an undo).
Its selection or caret moved, and the value did not.
Enter, in a field that submits.

The element's border box, in window coordinates: after the first paint with the
listener, then each time its size changes.

The element's scroll offset each time it moved: 0 at the start, negative as the content
moves.
A virtual list's visible rows: `start..end`.
The matches the element's `highlight` prop found, on screen or not.
A `motion` target was reached.

A looping animation is slowed, over its share of the frame; `compartment` is the
plugin's view it is drawn in.
The selected text changed: `None` when nothing is selected.
The window became the key window, or stopped being it.
Closing the window hid the app instead (it was the last window).
A modifier went down or up on its own.

Event.description:
One event, on `target`: an element that has a listener for it (`setEventListener`), or the
window. Window events have target 0, except the window's key and selection events, which have
the id the UI gave when it asked for them.

Point.description: A point in window coordinates, in pixels; or a distance, for a scroll's `delta`.

Modifiers.description: The modifier keys held. `cmd` is ⌘ on macOS and the Windows key elsewhere.

clickCount.description: 1, 2 or 3 for a single, double or triple click.

pressId.description:
Shared by every element's event of one press, innermost first, so a UI can stop it
propagating across them.

Press.description:
A mouse press or release. What a press does not know is `None`: an assistive technology's
click has no position.

keyChar.description: The character it types, if one: `"ß"` for ⌥s.

isHeld.description: Held down and repeating (key down only).

keystrokeId.description:
Shared by every element's event of one keystroke and the window's, so a UI can apply
`preventDefault` and `stopPropagation` across them.

Key.description: A key going down or up.

Selection.description:
A text field's selection as UTF-16 offsets into its value (the units JS strings use):
equal when it is only the caret. `end` is the caret unless it was selected backwards.
